guides.favoredWhen: Sett wins by timing Haymaker for the stun landing and bullying early; Jax wins if he blocks Q, sidesteps the W center, and avoids the level-6 throw.

keyTips.text: Time Haymaker as his stun is about to land. Hold W through Counter Strike and fire at expiry, turning his engage into your true-damage answer.
keyTips.heading: Stun timing

keyTips.text: Max W and take Conqueror or Grasp. The matchup turns on W hits rather than extended autos, so build the lane around the cooldown.
keyTips.heading: Setup

keyTips.text: Bully levels 1–3 while bulky. He concedes early brawls against your damage, so force health off him before his E timing sharpens.
keyTips.heading: Early bully

tips.text: Trade Q only after his E is spent. He blocks Q with Counter Strike, so bait the shield first and commit once it is down.
tips.heading: Q timing

tips.text: Take short brawls and reset. Never auto into an active E; hit and step out instead of offering the stunned exchange.
tips.heading: Short trades

tips.text: Bait E with Q feints before the R combo. Once the shield is gone, the full commit has no answer left.
tips.heading: Combo setup

tips.text: Aim W at his dodge exit. He sidesteps the center as you cast, so delay until Counter Strike expires and fire where he lands.
tips.heading: W placement

tips.text: Set up the throw toward your tower. After level 6, fight near your side so R drags him under the tower instead of across open ground.
tips.heading: R setup

tips.text: No W, no all-in. The cast is the kill condition, so disengage while it is down and re-engage only with it ready.
tips.heading: W discipline

itemization.text: Max W first and choose Conqueror or Grasp for the lane, since both key off the short-trade pattern into his shield timing.

guides.favoredWhen: Sett steals it by surviving her shorts, then turning one extended trade with stacked grit and a held Haymaker.

keyTips.text: Open Grasp with W max and a defensive setup. Answer her Q poke with a short of your own, then bank the grit instead of chasing into her kite.
keyTips.heading: Setup and stance

keyTips.text: Hold Haymaker for spent mobility. She dodges W with E or R, so fire the true-damage center only after her E or R is gone, or into her shroud exit.
keyTips.heading: Haymaker discipline

keyTips.text: Hold Facebreaker for her commit. Never throw E at max range into shroud; E her as she comes out of it, when she can no longer fade the pull.
keyTips.heading: Beating shroud

tips.text: Levels 1 to 3, meet her Q poke with a Q chase while the move speed lasts. Her rule is never auto-auto-Q early because you win the extended trade, so enforce exactly that whenever grit is ready.
tips.heading: Levels 1–3

tips.text: Stack Grasp on the wave without overextending. Each proc plus grit is the resource her short trades try to deny, so keep building it while refusing her kite.
tips.heading: Grasp banking

tips.text: Never burn both W and E on the wave. If either hits minions, she all-ins into the missing answer, so keep one cooldown held every single wave.
tips.heading: Cooldown banking

tips.text: When she shrouds defensively, hold center W for the fade. She must reappear, she cannot dodge forever, and the true-damage center punishes the exit.
tips.heading: Shroud timing

tips.text: With W max and Grasp stacked, force the extended fight she refuses: chase with Q, hold E for her E or R commitment, and finish with center W. One full-grit stat-check is the whole win condition.
tips.heading: The turn

guides.favoredWhen: Sett wins by baiting Riposte before pulling and landing full-grit Haymakers; Fiora wins if she holds W for W and kites his grit windows.

keyTips.text: Bait Riposte before using Facebreaker. If she parries the pull, your whole extended-trade plan falls apart, so show pressure until her W is gone.
keyTips.heading: Pull discipline

keyTips.text: Build early Bramble and armor boots and accept the volatile lane. Her vital procs out-trade you without armor, and the lane snowballs on the first kills.
keyTips.heading: Item setup

keyTips.text: Keep grit banked instead of spending Haymaker on the wave. She engages the moment your W is down, so a waved Haymaker is her all-in invitation.
keyTips.heading: Grit discipline

tips.text: Concede the bush level 1 and never face-check her opener. Her first auto Q from fog wins the all-in, so start on the wave and let her show first.
tips.heading: Level 1

tips.text: Level Q and run her down once her max-range poke is down. Her Q vital poke has to miss or be on cooldown before your Q move speed chase sticks.
tips.heading: Chasing her poke

tips.text: Pull her with E only after her Riposte is spent, then commit the full combo. An E into a held W gets stunned and turns your engage into her kill window.
tips.heading: Pull timing

tips.text: Aim Haymaker's true-damage center at the vital she is finishing. She commits position to complete each proc, and the center hitting her committed spot cannot be sidestepped.
tips.heading: Haymaker aim

tips.text: Carry her out of her ult healing with your ult before the last proc. If she starts R in the open, grabbing her mid-proc wastes the healing she positioned for.
tips.heading: Ult answer

tips.text: Force fights inside the wave where your grit stacks fastest. Away from minions she controls spacing with free Q pokes, but in the wave your W comes online first.
tips.heading: Wave fights

keyTips.text: Let the opponent's trade pattern choose the major rune, and make Sett's lane goal control enough of the wave to farm and stay useful rather than winning every exchange.
Line up Facebreaker with enemies on both sides of Sett to land the stun instead of only the slow, after sticking to the target with Knuckle Down's movement speed toward visible champions.
Wait for incoming damage before firing Haymaker with its Grit shield, aiming the cone's center at the target for the shield and true-damage payoff.

tips.text: Use the alternating punches' extra range and on-hit effects on the right punch to punish a step-up without overextending.
Save approach tools against kiters until Sett can actually stay on the target; walking in early lets them disengage for free.
Knuckle Down empowers the next two attacks and grants movement speed toward visible champions, so open with it once the all-in is real.
Build attack damage first and health close behind, since health feeds Haymaker's shield and damage pattern; add attack speed only when Sett can stay on targets.
Treat teamfighting as the stronger role: look for flanks or punish an enemy who steps too far forward, since a straight open-vision engage is easy to read.
Dive offensively or answer a dive: turret damage adds Grit, and the resulting shield plus crowd control wins the exchange under the tower.
Carry a frontline target into clustered enemies with The Show Stopper, whose slam damages and slows the area while scaling with the grabbed target's bonus health.
Ride the enemy frontline's commitment into the backline, then disrupt with Haymaker and Facebreaker once their engage is spent.

Reach ranged threats with a flank, Flash, or the ultimate instead of walking through their poke; Sett still matters late but loses some isolated-duel strength, where Blade of the Ruined King buys dueling at the cost of durability.

itemization.text: Run Conqueror with Triumph, Legend: Alacrity, Last Stand, Shield Bash, and Second Wind; take Lethal Tempo for sustained duels, Fleet Footwork into poke-and-disengage lanes, Grasp where it can trigger repeatedly, and never Hail of Blades.

Follow the bruiser damage path of Stridebreaker and Black Cleaver, the Blade of the Ruined King route, or the tankier Heartsteel and Titanic Hydra route; value movement speed for starting fights and skip critical strike and unreliable attack speed into kiters.
